name: Northshire Abbey
summary: Northshire Abbey trains the kingdom's newest defenders, in the foothills of Northshire Valley. It is the spiritual heart of the Brotherhood of Northshire. And for those who answer Stormwind's call, few schools in the land are finer. It has been built twice.

sections.title: A Legacy of Faith and Ruin
sections.body:
Centuries ago, clerics came south from Lordaeron to spread the Holy Light. They founded the Holy Order of Northshire Clerics, and they built its abbey. It soon became part of the life of the kingdom, caring for its sick. For years it tended the young Guardian Medivh, while he lay in his long coma.

Then the First War came. Brigands and the Horde struck at the abbey again and again, until it lay in ruins. In the Second War, the Alliance of Lordaeron freed the region. Afterward, Archbishop Alonsus Faol helped to raise the abbey anew. And he refounded its protectors as the Brotherhood of Northshire.

sections.title: The Training Grounds
sections.body:
Today the abbey takes in volunteers, militia recruits and novices, all of them hoping to defend Stormwind. In its halls, instructors teach the martial, arcane and holy arts. Scouts and rogues train out in the yards. And the Knights of the Silver Hand keep watch over it all.

But the peace here is fragile. Kobolds have overrun the nearby mines, and wolves prowl the orchards. Agents of the Defias Brotherhood stalk the valley roads. Not even the abbey's archives are safe from them. They steal its ancient scrolls and sacred librams.

faq.q: What is the Brotherhood of Northshire?
faq.answer: The Brotherhood of Northshire is a religious order of clerics, priests, and paladins based at Northshire Abbey. Clerics from Lordaeron founded it centuries ago, and Archbishop Alonsus Faol re-established it after the First War to train faithful defenders and preserve sacred scripture. Northshire Abbey stands in Elwynn Forest’s northern foothills.

faq.q: Why was Northshire Abbey destroyed in the First War?
faq.answer: During the First War, the abbey was important to Stormwind's defenses and faith. Orcish forces incited human brigands to attack, and after the half-orc Garona was briefly held captive there, a great Horde assault leveled the holy grounds. The abbey lay in ruins until the Alliance drove out the orcish clans and rebuilt it.

faq.q: Why are there Defias bandits and kobolds outside the abbey?
faq.answer: Stormwind's military is stretched thin protecting distant borders, leaving outlying regions poorly guarded. Kobolds have infested the local gold mines, while the Defias Brotherhood takes advantage of the gaps to rob travelers, harass local vineyards, and raid the abbey's library for arcane tomes and holy relics. Their agents steal ancient scrolls and sacred librams from the abbey’s archives.

faq.q: What is the connection between Northshire Abbey and the Deadmines?
faq.answer: During the First War, the ogre chieftain Turok stole the sacred Tome of Divinity from Northshire Abbey and retreated into the Deadmines. Sir Anduin Lothar led an expedition into the depths to recover it, became trapped, and was rescued by a royal party that returned the tome to the abbey.

angles.text: For humans of Stormwind, Northshire Abbey is where your journey begins, and where the kingdom's resilience and devotion welcome every recruit who takes up arms.
For a paladin, Northshire carries the legacy of Archbishop Alonsus Faol and the early clerics whose sacrifices laid the foundation for the Knights of the Silver Hand.
